summary: Fixed a bug where a normal myseliasan node-management session could trip the API rate limiter and appear to 'go online but can't load data'. The shared rate-limit middleware buckets by matched endpoint path, so myseliasan's node command-tunnel proxy (/api/nodes/{id}/proxy/...), which fans an entire node's UI (dashboard/cameras/settings/notifications) through one path, plus WebRTC live-view signaling and range-streamed recording playback (many Range requests per clip), were all collapsing into the single /api/nodes bucket. These three high-volume per-node surfaces are now exempted from the generic per-path limiter (isNodeFanoutPath in domain/utils/middlewares/rate_limit.go); node CRUD/adopt/release/wipe/access endpoints are unaffected and remain rate-limited normally. As further headroom, myseliasan's authOnly tier limit was also raised from 120 to 1200 requests per window.
compatibility: No API contract changes. The exempted surfaces are still authenticated and per-node-access-gated at their own handlers, and the node enforces its own limits downstream, so this does not reduce effective request authorization. Existing myseliasan installs get the fix automatically after upgrade; no config changes required (the authOnly.requests bump is already reflected in the shipped config.json/config.dev.json defaults, existing installs' own explicit values are untouched).
